finding.claim: GET /invoice/<inv_id> returns any invoice to any caller who knows its id. There is no ownership check.
finding.source: inv_id, taken from the URL path (line 8, route at line 7)
finding.sink: INVOICES.get(inv_id) (line 9) returns the full invoice, serialized by jsonify (line 10)

trace.note: @app.route("/invoice/<inv_id>") registers the route with no auth decorator
inv_id comes from the client path with no validation
INVOICES.get(inv_id) looks up by id only; g.user is never consulted
jsonify(inv) returns the record, including the customer field

finding.guards_checked: No before_request hook, decorator, or g.user check in this file; g.user is not referenced in this handler. The only guard is abort(404) for a missing id (line 9), which does not check ownership. Contrast with /my/invoice/<id> (lines 13-18), which compares inv["customer"] to g.user["id"] and returns 404 on mismatch, so it is correctly scoped. Precondition unverified: authentication may come from middleware outside this repo. If the app requires login, any logged-in user can read any other customer's invoice; if not, anyone can.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only checks are the abort(404) on a missing id at invoices.py:9, which is not an ownership check. The repo has no before_request hook, auth decorator, or login check, and g.user is only read at invoices.py:16 and :23 and never set in this repo. The ownership comparison exists only in get_my_invoice (invoices.py:16-17), not in get_invoice.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: the route at invoices.py:7 has no auth decorator, inv_id comes straight from the path at :8, INVOICES.get(inv_id) at :9 looks up by id alone, and jsonify(inv) at :10 returns the full record, while the customer check at :16-17 exists only in the sibling /my/invoice handler. Any caller the outer app lets reach this route, including a low-privilege customer, can read another customer's invoice; the one unverified point is whether external middleware outside this repo gates access, which would narrow the attacker to logged-in users but would not block the cross-customer read.
